assumptions.choice: Compute the 252-day highest close, then compare the current close against YESTERDAY's value of that indicator (self.high52(-1)) to detect the crossover.
assumptions.reason: If today's close is included in the 252-day window itself, a new-high day would make the indicator equal to today's close (since it becomes the max), so a true 'crosses above' event could never register. Comparing against the prior day's rolling high is the only literal reading that makes the stated crossover condition detectable.

assumptions.topic: 52-week high used for stop/limit while in position
assumptions.choice: Use the current bar's Highest(close, 252) value (self.high52[0], inclusive of today) as 'the most recent 52-week high' for computing 95%/90% levels each bar.
assumptions.reason: Spec says the stop-loss is updated based on the 'new'/'most recent' 52-week high, so the most up-to-date rolling value (including today's close) is used once already in a position.

assumptions.choice: Compute size = int(cash / close_price) and pass explicit size= to self.buy(), rather than the plain no-argument self.buy() canonical default.
assumptions.reason: Spec's Risk Management section explicitly states to assume a fixed position size of 100% of available capital per trade, which overrides the canonical no-size-argument default (that default only applies where the spec is silent).

assumptions.choice: Cancel any existing pending stop-limit order and resubmit a fresh one every bar while in position, using freshly computed stop/limit prices.
assumptions.reason: Backtrader has no native 'modify order' call; cancel-and-resubmit each bar is the literal way to implement 'continuously update the stop-loss order based on the new 52-week high.'

assumptions.choice: Implemented as a single sell order with exectype=bt.Order.StopLimit, price=95% of 52-week high (stop trigger), plimit=90% of 52-week high (limit fill).
assumptions.reason: This directly matches backtrader's built-in stop-limit order mechanics to the spec's description: triggers at the stop price, only fills at or better than the limit price.

assumptions.choice: No explicit buffer subtracted for the 0.1% commission when computing entry size from available cash.
assumptions.reason: Spec does not mention accounting for commission in sizing; occasional margin/rejection on the edge case where flooring leaves insufficient buffer is handled by the standard order-tracking guard and is not a scenario the spec addresses.
